policy: Public claims must name their scope, reason, evidence, and exclusions.

claims.claim: The canonical MIDI2 semantic schema is source-traceable.
claims.reason: All 67 schema definitions carry deliberate embedded MIDI Association provenance and declared verification metadata. This is object-to-source traceability; inverse corpus accounting is reported separately.
exclusions: This does not claim runtime implementation completeness or hardware interoperability.

claims.claim: The declared MIDI 2.0 corpus is represented as a complete machine-readable Fountain Coach object with no normative requirement excluded.
claims.reason: The full object joins structural schema/OpenAPI projections, twelve operational ledger entries, six behavioral models, and 1,316 source records. Every source record and every normalized requirement has a machine-resolvable representation; source hashes, versions, representations, generated reports, provenance, and mutation gates are verified in CI.

evidence.why: declared six-document corpus, versions, and source hashes
machine-readable representation for every extracted source record
machine-readable composition of structural and behavioral projections

exclusions: This does not claim runtime implementation completeness or physical hardware interoperability.
MIDI Association remains the normative authority for the represented corpus.

claims.claim: The closed schema and OpenAPI representation carry equivalent provenance metadata.
claims.reason: CI compares the embedded provenance entries for every shared schema definition.
exclusions: This is provenance parity, not a claim that both artifacts expose identical runtime behavior.

claims.claim: The provenance contract is protected by deterministic CI and mutation checks.
claims.reason: CI rejects missing or invalid provenance, missing verification references, OpenAPI drift, stale generated reports, and unannotated schema definitions.
exclusions: These checks verify the repository contract; they do not simulate physical MIDI2 devices.

claims.claim: The recorded validation run passed 354 Swift tests and 200 TypeScript tests, with one TypeScript test skipped.
claims.reason: The claim reports one identified local validation run rather than extrapolating from it to full conformance.
exclusions: Test counts are not a runtime-completeness percentage and are not hardware evidence.

claims.claim: Selected MIDI2 runtime features are implemented and tested, including UMP, MIDI-CI, Property Exchange, Stream/Function Block, and jitter-reduction paths.
claims.reason: The conformance checklist provides feature-level code and test references while explicitly recording remaining partial areas.
exclusions: No global claim of complete MIDI2 runtime implementation is made.
No hardware interoperability claim is made.

claims.claim: The declared owned core software surface is runtime-complete across the Swift and TypeScript implementations.
claims.reason: The machine-readable runtime boundary names the required protocol surfaces, marks each as verified, and is protected by Swift and TypeScript validation gates.

evidence.why: canonical runtime boundary and status ledger
machine-checks the ledger and hardware exclusion

exclusions: This is bounded to the named core software surface; it is not a claim that every optional MIDI2 extension or host adapter is implemented.
It does not claim physical MIDI2 hardware interoperability.

claims.reason: The repository has no physical MIDI2 devices or external-device acceptance evidence in scope.
exclusions: No claim about successful operation with physical MIDI2 hardware.
